                                             PILGANGOORA                                                                                             INTRODUCTION / OPERATIONS
                                                             Pilbara Minerals’ 100%-owned Pilgangoora Operation and Project (the Project)
                                                             is positioned close to key infrastructure (including road and port) and export
                                                             markets.
                                                             The Project is located on Wallareenya Station, which covers Nyamal and
                                                             Kariyarra country.
                                                             The Project comprises 34 granted tenements spanning 1086.42 square
                                                             kilometres (km2). It operates in accordance with Native Title Agreements,




For personal use only
                                             OPERATION AND
                                                             Pastoral Leases and Project Infrastructure Agreements, as well as relevant
                                                             national and state legal and other regulatory requirements. Additional detail
                                                             about the Project area is provided in the Sustainability section of this report.
                                                             The broader region hosts multiple mining and exploration leases and



                                                                                                                                                     SUSTAINABILITY
                                             PROJECT
                                                             operations that co-exist with pastoral, conservation and tourism sectors.




                                                                                                                                                     SUSTAINABLE OPERATIONS




       Pilbara Minerals 2022 ANNUAL REPORT
                                                                                                                                                     VALUE OUR PEOPLE




                                                             EXPLORATION AND GEOLOGY
                                                             The Project is strategically positioned within Western Australia’s resource-




                                                                                                                                                     RESPONSIBLE & ETHICAL ACTIONS
                                                             rich Pilbara region. The Company has a consolidated tenure within the
                                                             Pilgangoora pegmatite district within the Strelley, Tabba Tabba, Wodgina,
                                                             and Mount Francisco districts that together form part of one of the largest
                                                             rare-metal pegmatite provinces in the world. Most of the regional tenements
                                                             are greenfields opportunities that are prospective for a range of commodities
                                                             including rare-metals, gold and base metals.
                                                             During the year, Pilbara Minerals completed a strategic exploration and
                                                             resource development drilling program adjacent to the historical Altura
                                                             tenement boundary. The drilling campaign led to the discovery of new
                                                             pegmatite domains, and together with the integration of the existing
                                                             Ngungaju Mineral Resource and Ore Reserve resulted in substantial increases
                                                             to the Project’s Mineral Resource and Ore Reserve. Details of the exploration




                                                                                                                                                     FINANCIAL REPORT
                                                             program and subsequent Resource and Reserve statements were provided in
                                                             the Company’s ASX announcements dated 6 September 2021 and 6 October
                                                             2021. A significant resource development drilling is scheduled to commence in
                                                             the December 2022 Quarter.
                                                             The Company also completed a co-funded State Government Exploration
                                                             Incentive Scheme drilling program to test the depth extent of the Pilgangoora
                                                             rare-metal pegmatite system with results expected during the December 2022
                                                             Quarter.

                                             CASE STUDY
                                             INNOVATION IN TECHNOLOGY


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     RESPONSIBLE & ETHICAL ACTIONS
                                             In May 2022, Pilbara Minerals, and Calix, were awarded a $20M grant from the Australian Government under the
                                             Modern Manufacturing Initiative (MMI) – Manufacturing Translation Stream, supporting the further development and
                                             demonstration of the proposed Mid-stream Project.
                                             The grant is a vote of endorsement for this project and will be used to support the development of a demonstration scale
                                             chemicals facility at the Project under the proposed joint venture between Pilbara Minerals and Calix.
                                             The demonstration plant will exclusively utilise Calix’s innovative calciner technology for lithium processing applications,
                                             with the aim of producing lithium salts for global distribution via the innovative mid-steam “value added” refining
                                             process.
                                             The MMI grant will assist in proving up the technology proposed under the Mid-stream Project and has the potential to
                                             deliver significant benefits across the industry including:
                                               •   Increased downstream “value-add” realisation within the Australian economy and locally in the Pilbara region.




                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     FINANCIAL REPORT
                                               •   Significant sustainability benefits across the lithium industry via electrification of the “value-added” process
                                                   (including spodumene calcining), thereby enabling a decarbonisation pathway, as well as rationalisation of the
                                                   carbon footprint via reduced waste movements across transport and logistics supply chains from a near zero-
                                                   waste final product.
                                               •   Maximising hard-rock lithium resources via improved lithium recovery due to an efficient process of spodumene

                                             EMISSIONS REDUCTION: NET ZERO PATHWAY                                                                                                                                                                                                          (2040 Decade)
                                                                                                                                                                         Pathway to Net Zero
                                             Pilbara Minerals net zero pathway was developed in FY2021 based on outputs from a series of workshops with
                                             stakeholders. Pilbara Minerals’ Board and Sustainability Committee have played a pivotal role in ensuring the net zero




                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     VALUE OUR PEOPLE
                                             pathway options incorporate current and future growth. They have set an objective to embed emission reduction where         LIFE CYCLE ASSESSMENT
                                             practicable into every-day business and decision making to ensure the pathway can be achieved.
                                                                                                                                                                         In FY2022, Pilbara Minerals completed a life cycle assessment (LCA) to quantify the scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions within
                                             In FY2022, the net zero pathway was progressed and continues to be matured to identify the best fit pathway for the         its value chain. The work supported Pilbara Minerals’ approach to understand the source of its emissions and identify
                                             business. The following considerations are incorporated into the net zero pathway:                                          initiatives to further decarbonise its operations and areas within its value chain.
                                               •   Projected emissions profile of the Project (including expansion and efficiency projects).                             Pilbara Minerals worked with Minviro, global experts in battery metals LCA, to build ISO-compliant LCA models of the
                                               •   Alignment of emission reduction with a science-based emissions pathway.                                               mining, processing, transport and conversion process to produce a battery grade LHM product. This work incorporated
                                               •   Staged approach for implementation of abatement projects to align with technology.                                    various other scenarios including renewable energy applications and differing conversion processes. The intent of the
                                                                                                                                                                         LCA was to identify and quantify emissions and environmental impacts from the point of resource extraction (at the
                                               •   Development of interim and final targets.
                                                                                                                                                                         Project) to produce a battery grade LHM product at a chemical conversion facility in China.




                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     RESPONSIBLE & ETHICAL ACTIONS
                                             Initial efforts are focused on emissions reductions from plant and operation efficiencies. The subsequent emission
                                             reduction phases are more difficult to complete and will require a move from the current energy source (diesel) and
                                             adapting to a more efficient or renewable energy source. Pilbara Minerals is dedicated to meeting this challenge and will
                                             endeavour to implement the following initiatives to achieve its net zero goal.


                                             The net zero pathway breakdown:




                                                                                                                                                                         kg CO2 eq. per kg LIOH H20
                                               •   Early opportunities.
                                                   » Operational efficiencies – smaller scale renewable energy (6 MW solar plant), energy efficiencies within plant
                                                     and haulage operations.
                                                   » Mid-stream Project – construction of an interim lithia salts demonstration facility to advance the technical
                                                     development path of the technology.
                                               •   Mid-term opportunities.



                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     FINANCIAL REPORT
                                                   » Power generation – inclusion of alternative energy sources to offset diesel.
                                                   » Materials movement – materials movement fleet (haul/excavate/load) electrified and powered alternative
                                                     energy source to diesel.

                                             NYAMAL CAMP NAMES
                                             In early 2022, Pilbara Minerals worked with Nyamal representatives to rename accommodation blocks at the Carlindi
                                             Camp. The new names align with the Nyamal words for local fauna. The blocks are now known as: Joodu (Snake); Marloo
                                             (Kangaroo); Warringpirna (Wedgetail Eagle); and Nyamela (Pink Witchetty Grub).

                                                                                                                                                    Foreign Exchange Rates
                                                                                                                                                    Spodumene concentrate prices, tantalum prices and certain capital equipment purchases,




                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  RESPONSIBLE & ETHICAL ACTIONS
                                                                                                                                                    operating inputs and services relating to the Pilgangoora Project are denominated in US dollars, as
                                                                                                                                                    are the Company’s US$130 million senior secured debt facility and US$25 million working capital
                                                                                                                                                    facility (undrawn). Pilbara Minerals’ functional currency and most of its expenditure is and will be
                                                                                                                                                    taken into account in Australian dollars. This exposes Pilbara Minerals to fluctuations in foreign
                                                                                                                                                    currency exchange rates. There is a “natural” (but not perfect) hedge which matches to some degree
                                                                                                                                                    US denominated revenues with US debt and interest payments. The Company monitors foreign
                                                                                                                                                    exchange exposure risk on a regular basis through its treasury function and mitigated some of its
                                                                                                                                                    exposure to adverse foreign exchange movements during the year via foreign currency hedging
                                                                                                                                                    contracts for known foreign currency denominated cashflows.

                                             The Company’s People and Culture Committee (the PC Committee) is established by the Board
                                             under a formal charter which is comprised of three independent non-executive directors and is
                                                                                                                                                      Elements of Executive Remuneration
                                             chaired by Non-Executive Director, Nicholas Cernotta.

                                             The PC Committee assists the Board in fulfilling its corporate governance responsibilities in relation   The Company’s remuneration framework seeks to build a performance-based culture that supports
                                             to establishing and monitoring the effectiveness of the Company’s executive and non-executive            the strategic objectives of the Company and attract, retain and motivate employees by offering
                                             remuneration practices. It also advises the Board in relation to the Company’s culture, diversity and    market competitive remuneration and incentives.
                                             inclusion policies and practices and those related to the nomination and appointment of directors.




                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      RESPONSIBLE & ETHICAL ACTIONS
                                             The role of the PC Committee is to advise and make recommendations to the Board on
                                             remuneration arrangements for Executive and Non-Executive Directors and Other KMP in
                                             accordance with the Company’s Remuneration Policy. Each year the PC Committee makes
                                             recommendations to the Board on such remuneration arrangements, including fixed remuneration
                                             for executives and all awards and vesting of awards by way of STIs and LTI’s under the Company’s
                                             Award Plan.

                                             From time to time, the PC Committee engages independent external remuneration consultants to
                                             provide market related advice. The PC Committee engaged Guerdon Associates in March 2022 to
                                             conduct Board and Executive remuneration benchmarking reviews and to establish a peer group
                                             of companies for the purpose of relative total shareholder return (TSR) evaluations for the FY2023
                                             remuneration framework. The total fees paid to Guerdon Associates during the year to perform this



                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      FINANCIAL REPORT
                                             work was $61,206 excluding GST. No remuneration recommendations were provided by such
                                             consultants for the purposes of the Corporations Act 2001.

                                             Further information relating to the role of the PC Committee can be found in its Charter on the
                                             Company’s website.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      RESPONSIBLE & ETHICAL ACTIONS
                                             e.         Minimum holding condition policy
                                             All directors, executives and employees of the Company are encouraged to become equity holders
                                             and own Pilbara Minerals shares. To that end the Company enables executives and employees to
                                             participate in becoming shareholders or to increase their holdings through short term and long
                                             term incentives.

                                             The Company also has a minimum holding policy for KMP and the minimum holding requirements
                                             are as follows:
                                             •        Non-Executive Directors: equal to the value of annual base fees
                                             •        MD and CEO: equal to the value of annual fixed remuneration
                                             •        Other Executives: equal to half of the value of annual fixed remuneration




                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      FINANCIAL REPORT
                                             Participants are encouraged to meet their minimum shareholding within a reasonable timeframe
                                             over three years by holding shares or other securities that vest under any STI and LTI, or otherwise
                                             through on-market acquisition. The minimum shareholding requirement combined with the
                                             structure of the Company’s incentive plans ensures that KMP remuneration and their holdings in
                                             the Company are directly aligned with shareholder returns.

                                             All performance rights valuations during the period were performed by an independent third-party
                                             valuer. They are valued using the Monte Carlo simulation model (market based conditions) and the
                                             Black Scholes option valuation methodology (non-market based conditions) that takes into account                                  5.2    Loans and Borrowings
                                             the term of performance rights, the share price at grant date and expected volatility of the
                                             underlying share, the expected dividend yield, the risk free rate for the term of the right and the                                Accounting policy
                                             correlations and volatilities of the peer companies.                                                                               Borrowings
                                                                                                                                                                                Borrowings are initially measured at fair value less any directly attributable transaction costs.
                                                                                                                                                                                Subsequent to initial recognition, these liabilities are measured at amortised cost using the
                                                                                                                                                                                effective interest rate method.
                                                                                                                                                                                Borrowing costs directly attributable to the acquisition, construction or production of an asset that
                                                                                                                                                                                necessarily takes a substantial period of time to get ready for its intended use or sale are
                                                                                                                                                                                capitalised as part of the cost of the asset. All other borrowing costs are expensed in the period in
                                                                                                                                                                                which they occur. Borrowing costs consist of interest and other costs incurred in connection with
                                                                                                                                                                                the borrowing of funds. Investment income earned on the temporary investment of specific



                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               FINANCIAL REPORT
                                                                                                                                                                                borrowings pending their expenditure on qualifying assets is deducted from the borrowing costs
                                                                                                                                                                                eligible for capitalisation.

                                                                                                                                                                                Liabilities arising from contractual arrangements which contain leases are initially measured at

                                              The Group accounts for business combinations using the acquisition method when control is
                                              transferred to the Group. The consideration transferred in the acquisition is generally measured
                                              at fair value, as are the identifiable net assets acquired. Any goodwill that arises is tested annually
                                              for impairment. Any gain on a bargain purchase is recognised in profit or loss immediately.                6.4 Parent Entity Disclosures

                                              pre-existing relationships. Such amounts are generally recognised in profit and loss.
